One Identity Safeguard

capability 3.3 · readiness 3.4
  1. 20 Nov 2026 · permanent record
    First scored: capability 3.3, readiness 3.4
    The reasoning behind each of the seven scores
    • Capability and differentiation: 3.1
      Anchor 3: the product covers most of the six listed capabilities. Vaulting and rotation, session brokering and recording, just-in-time privilege and secrets for applications are shown in the administration guides and public code repositories. Endpoint privilege management rests on the product page only and is delivered by separately named products, and cloud entitlement management is outside the described scope. Anchor 4 needs all or nearly all capabilities shown in technical documentation; four of six are. How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (9)

  1. How many people will One Identity employ as an independent company, and how many work on Safeguard engineering and support?
    Headcount indicates the vendor's capacity to support the product through its separation from Quest.
  2. What was One Identity's revenue in its last financial year, and what share came from Safeguard?
    Revenue shows whether the business can fund the product on its own after separation.
  3. Has One Identity reduced its workforce in the last 24 months, including in connection with the separation from Quest, and by how much?
    Workforce reductions around a separation bear on support quality.
  4. Has One Identity or its parent been subject to any regulatory investigation, order or penalty in the last five years?
    Regulatory action against a privileged-access vendor bears on a bank's own supervisory standing.
  5. Is One Identity party to any pending or recently resolved litigation, and what is it about?
    Material litigation can affect the vendor during a change of ownership.
  6. Which vulnerabilities have been fixed in Safeguard for Privileged Passwords and Safeguard for Privileged Sessions in the last 24 months, was any exploited, and has One Identity had a security incident of its own?
    A privileged-access product holds the estate's most sensitive credentials; its vulnerability and incident record matters.
  7. Has One Identity lost any notable Safeguard customer in the last 24 months, and why?
    Customer departures can signal product or service problems.
  8. When did the current chief executive and executive team take up their roles, and were any departures contested?
    Leadership changes during a separation are a continuity risk.
  9. What are the licensing units and list prices for Safeguard for Privileged Passwords, Safeguard for Privileged Sessions and the hosted editions?
    Price and licensing units are needed to compare the product with alternatives.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-10 · launch One Identity
    One Identity releases Safeguard 9.0

    One Identity announced Safeguard 9.0 on 2026-11-10, comprising Safeguard for Privileged Passwords 9.0 and Safeguard for Privileged Sessions 9.0. The release moves to hardware-agnostic deployment, adds just-in-time group elevation scoped to an asset, ESXi account discovery and TLS 1.3 support. One Identity via CyberNewswire, carried on HackRead (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-06-25 · divestiture One Identity
    One Identity announces it will separate from Quest Software and base itself in Cork

    SecurityBrief (2026-06-25), ITPro and Biometric Update (2026-06-26) reported One Identity's announcement that it will operate as an independent company, separate from Quest Software, with its Cork, Ireland office as global headquarters. The company said the transition would continue through 2026. The owners of the independent company were not named in the coverage read, and completion was not confirmed.
